chapter_text:
CHAPTER 22 — कष्टं न्यासस्य रक्षणम् (KASHTAM NYASASYA RAKSHANAM — 'Guarding a Deposit is Hard')

Introduction — शूद्रकः मृच्छकटिकं च

This lesson is based on a famous episode from मृच्छकटिकम् (Mricchakatika, 'The Little Clay Cart'), one of the most beloved plays of classical Sanskrit literature. Its author is शूद्रकः (Shudraka), whom tradition remembers as a learned king — the prologue of the play itself praises him as a राजा who had mastered the Vedas, mathematics and the science of elephants. The play's name comes from मृत् (clay) + शकटिका (little cart) — a toy clay cart belonging to the hero's little son, which becomes a touching symbol of the family's poverty. मृच्छकटिकम् is a प्रकरणम् — a type of रूपक (drama) in which the plot is invented by the poet (कविकल्पित), the hero is an ordinary noble citizen such as a Brahmin or merchant (not a king or god), and the heroine may be a गणिका (courtesan). It has ten acts (दश अङ्काः) and is set in the great city of उज्जयिनी. Its realism — poor householders, thieves, gamblers, servants, judges — makes it unique among Sanskrit plays.

The main characters of our episode: चारुदत्तः — a Brahmin merchant of Ujjayini, once very wealthy but now poor because of his endless generosity (दानशीलता); his character (शीलम्) is the true wealth of the play. वसन्तसेना — a rich and noble-hearted गणिका who loves Charudatta for his virtues. मैत्रेयः — Charudatta's devoted friend, the विदूषकः (jester-companion). धूता — Charudatta's noble wife. शर्विलकः — a learned Brahmin youth who has taken to theft, in love with मदनिका, the maid (चेटी) of Vasantasena.

कः न्यासः? (What is a 'nyasa'?)

A न्यासः (also called निक्षेपः) is a deposit — valuables entrusted by one person to another for safekeeping, to be returned on demand. Accepting a न्यास is accepting a sacred trust (विश्वासः): dharma demands that the keeper guard it like his own life and, if it is lost, make it good from his own wealth. The title of our lesson — कष्टं न्यासस्य रक्षणम् — 'hard indeed is the guarding of a deposit' — echoes Charudatta's own anguished words in the play (कष्टं खलु न्यासस्य रक्षणम्).

कथा — The episode retold in simple Sanskrit

(1) उज्जयिन्यां नगर्यां चारुदत्तः नाम ब्राह्मणः वणिक् निवसति स्म। सः पूर्वं महाधनिकः आसीत्, किन्तु दानशीलतया सर्वं धनं याचकेभ्यः दत्त्वा दरिद्रः अभवत्। तथापि तस्य शीलं सौजन्यं च सर्वस्मिन् नगरे प्रसिद्धम् आसीत्। तस्य पत्नी धूता पतिव्रता आसीत्, मित्रं च मैत्रेयः नाम विदूषकः।
   Translation: In the city of Ujjayini there lived a Brahmin merchant named Charudatta. Formerly he was very rich, but by his habit of charity he gave away all his wealth to those who asked, and became poor. Even so, his character and courtesy were famous in the whole city. His wife was the devoted Dhuta, and his friend the jester Maitreya.
   शब्दार्थ: निवसति स्म = used to live; महाधनिकः = very wealthy; दानशीलतया = by (his) charitable nature; याचकेभ्यः = to beggars/askers; दरिद्रः = poor; शीलम् = character; सौजन्यम् = courtesy, goodness.

(2) एकदा रात्रौ वसन्तसेना नाम गणिका दुर्जनैः अनुधाविता चारुदत्तस्य गृहं शरणं प्रविष्टा। सा तस्य सज्जनतायां विश्वासं कृत्वा स्वकीयान् सुवर्णालङ्कारान् न्यासरूपेण तस्य हस्ते स्थापितवती — 'आर्य, एतान् अलङ्कारान् रक्षतु' इति। शरणागतायाः रक्षणं सज्जनानां धर्मः इति मत्वा चारुदत्तः तं न्यासं स्वीकृतवान्।
   Translation: One night the courtesan Vasantasena, chased by wicked men, entered Charudatta's house for refuge. Trusting his goodness, she placed her golden ornaments in his hands as a deposit — 'Noble sir, please guard these ornaments.' Thinking that protecting one who seeks refuge is the dharma of the good, Charudatta accepted the deposit.
   शब्दार्थ: अनुधाविता = chased, pursued; शरणम् = refuge; सुवर्णालङ्काराः = golden ornaments; न्यासरूपेण = in the form of a deposit; स्थापितवती = (she) placed; स्वीकृतवान् = accepted.

(3) अन्यस्यां रात्रौ शर्विलकः नाम ब्राह्मणयुवकः चौर्यार्थं चारुदत्तस्य जीर्णं गृहम् आगतवान्। सः वसन्तसेनायाः चेट्यां मदनिकायाम् अनुरक्तः आसीत्; तस्याः दास्यमोचनाय धनम् ऐच्छत्। सः चौर्यं शास्त्रम् इव मन्यते स्म — भित्तेः परीक्षां कृत्वा सन्धिच्छेदं कृत्वा च गृहं प्रविष्टः। तस्मिन् समये मैत्रेयः तत् सुवर्णभाण्डं हस्ते गृहीत्वा सुप्तः आसीत्। स्वप्नायमानः सः 'गृहाण एतत् सुवर्णभाण्डम्' इति वदन् भाण्डं शर्विलकस्य हस्ते एव दत्तवान्! शर्विलकः तत् गृहीत्वा निर्गतः।
   Translation: On another night a Brahmin youth named Sharvilaka came to Charudatta's ruined house to commit theft. He was in love with Madanika, Vasantasena's maid, and wanted money to buy her freedom from servitude. He regarded theft as if it were a science — examining the wall, cutting a breach (सन्धिच्छेद), he entered the house. At that time Maitreya was asleep holding the golden casket in his hand. Talking in his dream, saying 'take this golden casket', he placed the casket into Sharvilaka's very hands! Sharvilaka took it and left.
   शब्दार्थ: चौर्यार्थम् = for theft; जीर्णम् = old, ruined; अनुरक्तः = in love (with); दास्यमोचनाय = for release from servitude; भित्तिः = wall; सन्धिच्छेदः = cutting a breach (burglar's opening); सुवर्णभाण्डम् = golden casket; स्वप्नायमानः = dreaming, talking in sleep; निर्गतः = went out.

(4) प्रातःकाले चारुदत्तः न्यासस्य अपहरणं ज्ञात्वा अतीव व्यथितः अभवत् — 'हा कष्टम्! वसन्तसेनायाः न्यासः मम गृहात् अपहृतः। दरिद्रस्य मम वचनं कः श्रद्धास्यति? जनाः वदिष्यन्ति — दारिद्र्यपीडितः चारुदत्तः एव न्यासम् अपहृतवान् इति। धनं नश्यतु नाम, मम सत्यं शीलं च न नश्येत्।' कष्टं खलु न्यासस्य रक्षणम्!
   Translation: In the morning, learning that the deposit had been stolen, Charudatta was deeply anguished — 'Alas! Vasantasena's deposit has been stolen from my house. Who will believe the word of a poor man like me? People will say: it was Charudatta himself, tormented by poverty, who took the deposit. Let the wealth perish — but let not my truth and character perish.' Hard indeed is the guarding of a deposit!
   शब्दार्थ: अपहरणम् = theft, carrying away; व्यथितः = pained; अपहृतः = stolen; श्रद्धास्यति = will believe; दारिद्र्यपीडितः = tormented by poverty; नश्यतु नाम = let it perish by all means.

(5) तदा धूता स्वस्य बहुमूल्यां रत्नावलीं आनीय पत्युः समीपं प्रेषितवती — 'इयं रत्नावली न्यासस्य स्थाने वसन्तसेनायै दीयताम्' इति। भार्यायाः त्यागं दृष्ट्वा चारुदत्तः गद्गदः अभवत्। सः मैत्रेयद्वारा तां रत्नावलीं वसन्तसेनायै प्रेषितवान्। एवं दरिद्रः अपि सः न्यासस्य मूल्यं प्रत्यर्पितवान्।
   Translation: Then Dhuta brought her own precious pearl-and-jewel necklace (ratnavali) and sent it to her husband — 'let this necklace be given to Vasantasena in place of the deposit.' Seeing his wife's sacrifice Charudatta was choked with emotion. Through Maitreya he sent the necklace to Vasantasena. Thus, though poor, he made good the value of the deposit.
   शब्दार्थ: बहुमूल्या = very precious; रत्नावली = necklace of jewels/pearls; त्यागः = sacrifice; गद्गदः = choked with emotion; प्रत्यर्पितवान् = returned, made restitution.

(6) इतः शर्विलकः तान् अलङ्कारान् मदनिकायै दर्शितवान्। सा स्वस्वामिन्याः अलङ्कारान् परिचित्य भीता अभवत् — 'एते वसन्तसेनायाः अलङ्काराः! त्वं सज्जनस्य चारुदत्तस्य गृहात् एतान् अपहृतवान्। तस्य अपवादः मा भूत्। एतान् वसन्तसेनायै प्रत्यर्पय' इति सा उक्तवती। शर्विलकः तथा एव कृतवान्। वसन्तसेना सर्वं वृत्तान्तं ज्ञात्वा मदनिकां दास्यात् मोचितवती। एवं सत्यं शीलं च अन्ते विजयते।
   Translation: Meanwhile Sharvilaka showed the ornaments to Madanika. Recognising her mistress's ornaments she was frightened — 'These are Vasantasena's ornaments! You have stolen them from the house of the good Charudatta. Let no blame fall on him. Return them to Vasantasena.' Sharvilaka did exactly so. Vasantasena, learning the whole story, freed Madanika from servitude. Thus truth and character triumph in the end.
   शब्दार्थ: परिचित्य = having recognised; अपवादः = blame, ill-repute; मा भूत् = let it not be; प्रत्यर्पय = return!; वृत्तान्तः = account, story; मोचितवती = (she) freed.

श्लोकाः — Two famous verses of Charudatta (from Mricchakatika, Act 1)

Verse 1:
   दारिद्र्यान्मरणाद् वा मरणं मम रोचते न दारिद्र्यम् ।
   अल्पक्लेशं मरणं दारिद्र्यमनन्तकं दुःखम् ॥
   अन्वयः: दारिद्र्यात् मरणात् वा (मध्ये) मम मरणं रोचते, न दारिद्र्यम्; मरणम् अल्पक्लेशम्, दारिद्र्यम् (तु) अनन्तकं दुःखम्।
   शब्दार्थ: दारिद्र्यात् = than poverty; मरणात् = than death; वा = or; रोचते = pleases; अल्पक्लेशम् = of little pain; अनन्तकम् = endless; दुःखम् = sorrow.
   Translation: Between poverty and death, death pleases me more, not poverty; death is a brief pain, but poverty is endless sorrow.
   भावः: Charudatta does not fear the loss of comforts; he grieves because poverty is a living, unending humiliation for a self-respecting, generous man — while death hurts only once.

Verse 2:
   सत्यं न मे विभवनाशकृतास्ति चिन्ता भाग्यक्रमेण हि धनानि भवन्ति यान्ति ।
   एतत्तु मां दहति नष्टधनाश्रयस्य यत्सौहृदादपि जनाः शिथिलीभवन्ति ॥
   अन्वयः: सत्यं मे विभवनाशकृता चिन्ता न अस्ति; हि धनानि भाग्यक्रमेण भवन्ति यान्ति (च)। तु एतत् मां दहति यत् नष्टधनाश्रयस्य (जनस्य) सौहृदात् अपि जनाः शिथिलीभवन्ति।
   शब्दार्थ: विभवनाशकृता = caused by loss of wealth; चिन्ता = worry; भाग्यक्रमेण = by the turns of fortune; भवन्ति यान्ति = come and go; दहति = burns; नष्टधनाश्रयस्य = of one whose wealth (support) is lost; सौहृदात् = from friendship; शिथिलीभवन्ति = become slack, grow cold.
   Translation: Truly I have no worry caused by the loss of wealth — riches come and go by the turns of fortune. But this burns me: that when a man's wealth is gone, people grow cold even in friendship.
   भावः: The verse reveals Charudatta's nobility — his pain is not for gold but for the loss of warmth, trust and respect that poverty brings.

नीतिः — The moral of the lesson

1. A न्यास is a sacred trust: accepting it means guarding it like one's own life, and restoring its value if it is lost — as Charudatta did with Dhuta's ratnavali. 2. Honesty shines brightest in poverty: Charudatta had every excuse to do nothing, yet he chose restitution over reputation-saving silence. 3. Trust once broken burns more than lost gold — Charudatta feared the loss of विश्वास and यशः, not of wealth. 4. Even the wrongdoer can turn back: Sharvilaka, guided by Madanika, returned what he stole. 5. कष्टं खलु न्यासस्य रक्षणम् — responsibility for what others entrust to us (money, secrets, duties) is a heavy burden that only the honest can carry.

व्याकरणम् — Grammar from the lesson

(A) सन्धिः: दारिद्र्यान्मरणात् = दारिद्र्यात् + मरणात् (त् before म् becomes न् — व्यञ्जनसन्धिः, as in तत् + मात्रम् → तन्मात्रम्); नास्ति = न + अस्ति (अ + अ = आ, दीर्घसन्धिः); चास्ति = च + अस्ति; यत्सौहृदात् = यत् + सौहृदात्; एतत्तु = एतत् + तु; कष्टं खलु — the अनुस्वार म् before ख; स्वीकृतवान् = सु? no — स्वी + कृतवान् (साधित रूप). Practise सन्धिविच्छेद: मृच्छकटिकम् = मृत् + शकटिका (त् + श् → च्छ्, श्चुत्वसन्धिः)।

(B) समासः: न्यासरक्षणम् = न्यासस्य रक्षणम् (षष्ठीतत्पुरुषः); सुवर्णभाण्डम् = सुवर्णस्य भाण्डम् (षष्ठीतत्पुरुषः); विभवनाशः = विभवस्य नाशः (षष्ठीतत्पुरुषः); दारिद्र्यपीडितः = दारिद्र्येण पीडितः (तृतीयातत्पुरुषः); नष्टधनः = नष्टं धनं यस्य सः (बहुव्रीहिः); ब्राह्मणयुवकः = ब्राह्मणः (चासौ) युवकः (कर्मधारयः)।

(C) विभक्तिः: न्यासस्य (षष्ठी — of the deposit); गृहे / नगर्याम् (सप्तमी — in); चौरेण / दानशीलतया (तृतीया — by); वसन्तसेनायै / मदनिकायै (चतुर्थी — for/to); दारिद्र्यात् / गृहात् (पञ्चमी — from/than); अलङ्कारान् (द्वितीया — object)।

(D) लकाराः: रक्षति (लट् — present); अरक्षत् (लङ् — past); रक्षिष्यति / श्रद्धास्यति / वदिष्यन्ति (लृट् — future); रक्षतु / प्रत्यर्पय / दीयताम् (लोट् — command/request); रक्षेत् / न नश्येत् (विधिलिङ् — should/may). In रोचते and मन्यते the verbs are आत्मनेपद forms of लट्।

सारांशः (Summary)

In this chapter you met Shudraka's मृच्छकटिकम्, a ten-act प्रकरण set in Ujjayini, and its noble hero Charudatta — poor in wealth, rich in character. Vasantasena entrusted her golden ornaments to him as a न्यास; Sharvilaka stole them by सन्धिच्छेद to free his beloved Madanika; Charudatta, fearing not the loss of gold but the loss of trust, resolved to make the deposit good, and Dhuta gave her own ratnavali for it. Madanika's counsel turned even the thief toward restitution, and truth triumphed. Two immortal verses showed that poverty is an endless sorrow chiefly because it loosens friendship and trust. From the text you also learned सन्धि (दारिद्र्यान्मरणात्), समास (न्यासरक्षणम्, नष्टधनः), विभक्ति and the लकाराः. Remember: कष्टं खलु न्यासस्य रक्षणम् — yet guarding a trust, however hard, is the mark of the truly noble.

topics.name: शूद्रकः मृच्छकटिकं च — Shudraka and the Mricchakatika
topics.description: Introduction to the playwright Shudraka (traditionally a learned king) and his ten-act play मृच्छकटिकम् ('The Little Clay Cart'), a प्रकरण set in Ujjayini, famous for its realism and its ordinary-life hero.

topics.name: न्यासकथा — The Deposit Episode
topics.description: The story of the न्यास: Vasantasena entrusts her golden ornaments to Charudatta for safekeeping; the sequence of events from the deposit through the theft to the restitution with Dhuta's ratnavali.

topics.name: शर्विलकः चौर्यं च — Sharvilaka and the Theft
topics.description: The Brahmin youth Sharvilaka who treats burglary as a science, enters Charudatta's house by सन्धिच्छेद (cutting a breach) to win money for Madanika's freedom, and his later change of heart.

topics.name: चारुदत्तस्य शीलम् — Charudatta's Character and Dhuta's Sacrifice
topics.description: Charudatta's anguish at the stolen trust, his fear that a poor man will not be believed, his resolve to restore the deposit, and Dhuta's sacrifice of her own ratnavali — honesty and nobility in poverty.

topics.name: शब्दार्थः श्लोकाश्च — Word Meanings and Selected Verses
topics.description: Vocabulary of the lesson (न्यासः, सन्धिच्छेदः, रत्नावली, अपवादः...) and the two famous verses of Charudatta — दारिद्र्यान्मरणाद् वा and सत्यं न मे विभवनाशकृतास्ति चिन्ता — with शब्दार्थ, अन्वय and meaning.

topics.name: व्याकरणम् — Grammar from the Lesson
topics.description: Grammar drawn from the text: सन्धि and सन्धिविच्छेद (दारिद्र्यान्मरणात्, मृच्छकटिकम्), समास types (तत्पुरुष, कर्मधारय, बहुव्रीहि), विभक्ति usage, and the लकाराः (लट्, लङ्, लृट्, लोट्, विधिलिङ्).

learning_outcomes.topic_name: शूद्रकः मृच्छकटिकं च — Shudraka and the Mricchakatika
learning_outcomes.description: Describe the playwright Shudraka and the play मृच्छकटिकम् — its title meaning, ten-act structure, setting in Ujjayini — and explain the features of a प्रकरण as a dramatic type.
Recall the characters (Charudatta, Vasantasena, Maitreya, Dhuta, Sharvilaka, Madanika) and narrate the sequence of the deposit episode from entrustment to theft to restitution.
Explain the concept of न्यास (deposit held in trust), the dharma of guarding and restoring it, and the meaning of the title कष्टं न्यासस्य रक्षणम्.

chapter_summary.title: कष्टं न्यासस्य रक्षणम् — Chapter Summary
chapter_summary.intro: This NIOS Senior Secondary Sanskrit (309) summary covers Chapter 22, based on the deposit episode of Shudraka's मृच्छकटिकम्: Vasantasena's golden ornaments entrusted to the poor but honest Charudatta, their theft by Sharvilaka, and the restitution that proves character is greater wealth than gold.

branches.label: नाटककारः — Shudraka & the play
details: प्रकरणम् in 10 acts, set in उज्जयिनी

branches.label: कथा — The episode
details: Sharvilaka enters by सन्धिच्छेद and steals them
