Poverty's real pain: friends grow cold
Even a wrongdoer can return to dharma

sections.heading: Shudraka, Mricchakatika and the prakarana form
bullets: मृच्छकटिकम् ('The Little Clay Cart') is a ten-act Sanskrit play by शूद्रक, whom tradition remembers as a learned king; it is set in the city of उज्जयिनी.
It is a प्रकरणम् — a drama whose plot is invented by the poet, whose hero is an ordinary noble citizen (here a poor Brahmin merchant), and whose heroine may be a गणिका.
The play is loved for its realism — poor households, thieves, servants, gamblers and judges appear on stage — rare in classical Sanskrit drama.
The title refers to the hero's son's toy cart of clay, a symbol of the family's poverty and dignity.

sections.heading: The deposit and the theft
bullets: Vasantasena, seeking refuge in Charudatta's house, entrusts her golden ornaments to him as a न्यास (deposit), trusting his famed honesty.
Sharvilaka, a learned Brahmin turned thief for the sake of freeing his beloved Madanika, breaks into the house at night by सन्धिच्छेद (cutting a breach in the wall), treating theft like a science.
In a scene of dramatic irony, the sleeping Maitreya — dreaming — hands the golden casket straight into the thief's hands.
Sharvilaka escapes with the ornaments, leaving the household unaware until morning.

sections.heading: Charudatta's anguish and the restitution
bullets: Discovering the theft, Charudatta grieves not for the gold but for the broken trust: 'who will believe a poor man?' — people will say poverty made him take the deposit himself.
His cry कष्टं खलु न्यासस्य रक्षणम् gives the lesson its title: guarding what others entrust is a heavy burden.
Dhuta gives her own precious रत्नावली so that the deposit's value can be restored to Vasantasena — nobility answering nobility.
Madanika, recognising her mistress's ornaments, makes Sharvilaka return them; Vasantasena frees Madanika, and truth triumphs.

sections.heading: The two verses and their message
bullets: दारिद्र्यान्मरणाद् वा...: between poverty and death Charudatta prefers death — death is brief pain, poverty an endless sorrow.
सत्यं न मे विभवनाशकृतास्ति चिन्ता...: he does not mourn lost riches, which come and go by fate; what burns him is that friends grow cold toward a man whose wealth is gone.
Together the verses show that poverty's deepest wound is the loss of trust, respect and warmth — not the loss of comforts.
They also reveal the hero's नोबल outlook: wealth is fortune's toy, but शीलम् (character) is one's own.

sections.heading: Grammar from the lesson
bullets: सन्धिः: दारिद्र्यान्मरणात् = दारिद्र्यात् + मरणात् (त् → न् before म्); नास्ति = न + अस्ति; मृच्छकटिकम् = मृत् + शकटिका (श्चुत्वसन्धिः).
समासः: न्यासरक्षणम् = न्यासस्य रक्षणम् (षष्ठीतत्पुरुषः); दारिद्र्यपीडितः (तृतीयातत्पुरुषः); नष्टधनः = नष्टं धनं यस्य सः (बहुव्रीहिः).
विभक्तिः: न्यासस्य (षष्ठी), गृहे/नगर्याम् (सप्तमी), चौरेण (तृतीया), वसन्तसेनायै (चतुर्थी), गृहात् (पञ्चमी).
लकाराः: रक्षति (लट्), अरक्षत् (लङ्), रक्षिष्यति (लृट्), रक्षतु/प्रत्यर्पय (लोट्), रक्षेत् (विधिलिङ्).

key_takeaways: मृच्छकटिकम् by शूद्रक is a ten-act प्रकरण set in Ujjayini, famous for its realistic, ordinary-life characters.
A न्यास (deposit) is a sacred trust: dharma requires guarding it like one's own life and restoring its value if lost.
Charudatta grieved for the broken trust and his imperilled good name, not for the lost gold — कष्टं खलु न्यासस्य रक्षणम्.
Dhuta's gift of her रत्नावली shows that restitution and honour mattered more to the family than their last wealth.
Sharvilaka's return of the ornaments, guided by Madanika, shows that even a wrongdoer can come back to dharma.
The verses teach that poverty's real sorrow is endless humiliation and cooling friendships, not mere lack of comforts.
From the text: सन्धि (दारिद्र्यान्मरणात्), समास (न्यासरक्षणम्, नष्टधनः), विभक्ति and लकार identification.

glossary.definition: A deposit; valuables entrusted to someone for safekeeping, to be guarded faithfully and returned on demand (synonym: निक्षेपः).
A type of Sanskrit drama with an invented plot and an ordinary noble hero (Brahmin/merchant); मृच्छकटिकम् is its most famous example.
'The Little Clay Cart' (मृत् + शकटिका) — Shudraka's ten-act प्रकरण; named after the hero's son's toy clay cart.
A courtesan; in the play Vasantasena, a wealthy and noble-hearted गणिका of Ujjayini who loves Charudatta for his virtues.
The hero's jester-companion in Sanskrit drama; here मैत्रेयः, Charudatta's devoted friend who sleeps holding the casket.
A burglar's breach — cutting an opening in a house wall to enter; Sharvilaka's 'scientific' method of entry.
A necklace of jewels/pearls; Dhuta's own precious necklace, given to restore the value of the stolen deposit.
Poverty; in Charudatta's verse an 'endless sorrow' (अनन्तकं दुःखम्) worse than death, which is only a brief pain.
Character, moral conduct; Charudatta's true wealth, which he refuses to lose even when all his money is gone.
Blame, ill-repute, false accusation; what Charudatta fears — that people will say the poor man stole the deposit himself.
One who has come for refuge; protecting such a person is the dharma of the good — why Charudatta accepted the deposit.
Friendship, warm-heartedness; in verse 2 even सौहृद grows cold (शिथिलीभवन्ति) toward a man who has lost his wealth.
A tatpurusha compound whose first member carries a genitive sense, e.g. न्यासरक्षणम् = न्यासस्य रक्षणम्.
A compound naming something outside itself, e.g. नष्टधनः = नष्टं धनं यस्य सः (one whose wealth is lost).
A tense/mood class of the Sanskrit verb: लट् (present), लङ् (past), लृट् (future), लोट् (command), विधिलिङ् (should).

worksheet.title: Worksheet — कष्टं न्यासस्य रक्षणम् (NIOS Sanskrit 309, Chapter 22)
worksheet.instructions: Attempt all questions. Write Sanskrit words in Devanagari and explanations in English. Refer to the prose passages and verses of the lesson where needed.

questions.question: Translate and explain: 'कष्टं खलु न्यासस्य रक्षणम्।' Who feels this in the lesson, and why?
questions.answer: Translation: 'Hard indeed is the guarding of a deposit.' Charudatta feels this after Vasantasena's golden ornaments, kept with him as a न्यास, are stolen from his house. Guarding a deposit is hard because the keeper carries full responsibility: if it is lost, he must restore it, and — being poor — he fears no one will believe he did not take it himself.
questions.explanation: The line gives the chapter its title and sums up the burden of a trust.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ (English meaning) of: न्यासः, सन्धिच्छेदः, रत्नावली, अपवादः, गद्गदः.
questions.answer: न्यासः = a deposit kept in trust; सन्धिच्छेदः = a burglar's breach cut in a wall; रत्नावली = a necklace of jewels/pearls; अपवादः = blame, ill-repute; गद्गदः = choked with emotion.
questions.explanation: Key vocabulary from the prose passages of the lesson.

questions.question: Who deposited what with Charudatta, and why did she choose him?
questions.answer: Vasantasena, the noble-hearted गणिका of Ujjayini, deposited her golden ornaments (सुवर्णालङ्काराः, in a golden casket) with Charudatta as a न्यास. Chased by wicked men, she took refuge in his house and chose him because his honesty and good character (शीलम्) were famous in the whole city.
questions.explanation: Recall of the entrustment scene.

questions.question: Do the सन्धिविच्छेद of: (a) दारिद्र्यान्मरणात् (b) नास्ति, and name each sandhi.
questions.answer: (a) दारिद्र्यान्मरणात् = दारिद्र्यात् + मरणात् — the final त् becomes न् before म् (व्यञ्जनसन्धिः, as in तत् + मात्रम् = तन्मात्रम्). (b) नास्ति = न + अस्ति — अ + अ = आ (दीर्घसन्धिः).
questions.explanation: Both forms occur in the verses/prose of the lesson.

questions.question: Give the समासविग्रह and name the samasa: (a) न्यासरक्षणम् (b) नष्टधनः.
questions.answer: (a) न्यासरक्षणम् = न्यासस्य रक्षणम् — षष्ठीतत्पुरुषः. (b) नष्टधनः = नष्टं धनं यस्य सः — बहुव्रीहिः (one whose wealth is lost).
questions.explanation: Tatpurusha resolves with a case relation; bahuvrihi points to an outside possessor.

questions.question: Narrate the न्यास episode of the lesson in proper sequence, from Vasantasena's deposit to the freeing of Madanika, naming all the characters involved.
questions.answer: 1. Vasantasena, pursued at night, takes refuge in Charudatta's house in Ujjayini and entrusts her golden ornaments to him as a न्यास, trusting his famed honesty. 2. Sharvilaka, a learned Brahmin turned thief to free his beloved Madanika (Vasantasena's maid) from servitude, cuts a breach (सन्धिच्छेद) in the wall of Charudatta's old house at night. 3. Maitreya, sleeping with the golden casket in his hand, dreamily hands it to Sharvilaka, who escapes with it. 4. In the morning Charudatta is anguished — not for the gold but for the broken trust — fearing that no one will believe a poor man. 5. His wife Dhuta gives her own precious रत्नावली so that the deposit's value may be restored; Maitreya carries it to Vasantasena. 6. Meanwhile Madanika recognises her mistress's ornaments, rebukes Sharvilaka and makes him return them to Vasantasena. 7. Vasantasena, learning everything, frees Madanika. Truth and character triumph.
questions.explanation: Full sequence: deposit → theft → anguish → restitution → return → freedom.

questions.question: Write the अन्वय, शब्दार्थ and meaning of the verse: दारिद्र्यान्मरणाद् वा मरणं मम रोचते न दारिद्र्यम् । अल्पक्लेशं मरणं दारिद्र्यमनन्तकं दुःखम् ॥ What does it reveal about Charudatta?
questions.answer: अन्वयः: दारिद्र्यात् मरणात् वा (मध्ये) मम मरणं रोचते, न दारिद्र्यम्; मरणम् अल्पक्लेशम्, दारिद्र्यम् (तु) अनन्तकं दुःखम्। शब्दार्थ: दारिद्र्यात् = than poverty; मरणात् = than death; रोचते = pleases; अल्पक्लेशम् = of little pain; अनन्तकम् = endless; दुःखम् = sorrow. Meaning: Between poverty and death, death pleases me more, not poverty; death is a brief pain, but poverty is an endless sorrow. It reveals Charudatta's self-respect and sensitivity: for a generous man, poverty is a living humiliation — he cannot give, and people doubt and desert him — whereas death hurts only once. It is grief over lost dignity and trust, not over lost comforts.
questions.explanation: Anvaya rearranges the verse into prose order; the bhava is the endlessness of poverty's pain.

questions.question: What contradiction do we see in Sharvilaka's character? How does the episode resolve it?
questions.answer: Sharvilaka is a learned Brahmin — expected to live by dharma — yet he practises theft, even treating it like a science (examining the wall, cutting a neat सन्धिच्छेद). His motive is love: he wants money to free Madanika from servitude. The contradiction is resolved when Madanika, recognising Vasantasena's ornaments, rebukes him; he returns the stolen ornaments, protecting Charudatta's good name, and thus comes back toward dharma.
questions.explanation: Learning vs conduct; love as motive; restitution as return to dharma.

questions.question: Was Dhuta right to give away her रत्नावली? Give a reasoned judgement.
questions.answer: Yes. The deposit was lost from her household, so restoring its value was the family's dharma. The ratnavali was her own precious possession, yet she valued the family's honour and Vasantasena's trust above ornaments. Her quiet sacrifice matches her husband's honesty — showing that in this family character is counted greater wealth than gold.
questions.explanation: Evaluation question: dharma of restitution and the worth of honour over wealth.

questions.question: A friend leaves her laptop with you for a week and it is stolen despite your care. Using the lesson, what should you do and why?
questions.answer: Like Charudatta, I should tell my friend the truth at once, take responsibility, and make the loss good as far as I can (repair, replace or repay), even at personal cost. The lesson teaches that a deposit is a sacred trust: guarding it is hard (कष्टं न्यासस्य रक्षणम्), but the keeper's honesty and the owner's trust matter more than the thing lost.
questions.explanation: Application of the moral of restitution and trust to daily life.

questions.question: मृच्छकटिकम् इति रूपकस्य रचयिता कः? (Who is the author of Mricchakatika?)
questions.answer: शूद्रकः
questions.explanation: मृच्छकटिकम् was composed by Shudraka, whom tradition remembers as a learned king.

questions.question: मृच्छकटिकम् is which type of रूपक (drama)?
questions.answer: प्रकरणम्
questions.explanation: It is a प्रकरण — invented plot, ordinary noble hero (a merchant-Brahmin), heroine a गणिका.

questions.question: The title मृच्छकटिकम् means:
questions.answer: The Little Clay Cart
questions.explanation: मृत् (clay) + शकटिका (little cart) — the toy cart of Charudatta's young son.

questions.question: मृच्छकटिके कति अङ्काः सन्ति? (How many acts does Mricchakatika have?)
questions.explanation: Mricchakatika is a ten-act प्रकरण.

questions.question: The story of the lesson takes place in which city?
questions.answer: उज्जयिनी
questions.explanation: Charudatta and Vasantasena live in the great city of Ujjayini.

questions.question: Which feature marks मृच्छकटिकम् as a प्रकरण rather than a नाटक?
options: Its hero is a god or famous king from legend
Its plot is taken from the Ramayana
Its plot is poet-invented and its hero is an ordinary noble citizen
questions.answer: Its plot is poet-invented and its hero is an ordinary noble citizen
questions.explanation: A प्रकरण has a कविकल्पित plot and a hero like a Brahmin or merchant; a नाटक takes a famous legendary hero.

questions.question: Tradition describes the playwright शूद्रक as:
questions.answer: a learned king
questions.explanation: The play's prologue praises Shudraka as a राजा learned in the Vedas, mathematics and elephant-lore.

questions.question: मृच्छकटिकम् इति पदस्य सन्धिविच्छेदः कः?
questions.answer: मृत् + शकटिका
questions.explanation: त् + श् → च्छ् (श्चुत्वसन्धिः): मृत् (clay) + शकटिका (little cart).

questions.question: Why is मृच्छकटिकम् considered unusually realistic among Sanskrit plays?
options: It shows only gods and sages
It stages poor households, thieves, gamblers, servants and judges
It is written entirely in Vedic Sanskrit
questions.answer: It stages poor households, thieves, gamblers, servants and judges
questions.explanation: Its ordinary-life characters and social realism make it unique in classical Sanskrit drama.

questions.question: The lesson कष्टं न्यासस्य रक्षणम् is based on which episode of the play?
options: The gambling scene in the court
The theft of Vasantasena's ornaments deposited with Charudatta
The storm scene in the garden
questions.answer: The theft of Vasantasena's ornaments deposited with Charudatta
questions.explanation: The chapter retells the न्यास (deposit) episode — entrustment, theft by Sharvilaka, and restitution.

questions.question: कः स्वालङ्कारान् न्यासरूपेण स्थापितवती? (Who placed her ornaments as a deposit?)
questions.answer: वसन्तसेना
questions.explanation: Vasantasena entrusted her golden ornaments to Charudatta as a न्यास.

questions.question: वसन्तसेना कस्य हस्ते न्यासं स्थापितवती? (With whom did Vasantasena keep the deposit?)
questions.answer: चारुदत्तस्य
questions.explanation: She trusted the famously honest Charudatta with her ornaments.

questions.question: What exactly was the न्यास in the lesson?
questions.answer: golden ornaments in a casket
questions.explanation: Vasantasena's सुवर्णालङ्काराः, kept in a golden casket (सुवर्णभाण्डम्).

questions.question: न्यासस्य चौर्यं कः अकरोत्? (Who committed the theft of the deposit?)
questions.answer: शर्विलकः
questions.explanation: Sharvilaka, the Brahmin youth, stole the casket from Charudatta's house at night.

questions.question: How did the thief enter Charudatta's house?
options: by cutting a breach in the wall (सन्धिच्छेद)
questions.answer: by cutting a breach in the wall (सन्धिच्छेद)
questions.explanation: Sharvilaka examined the wall and cut a burglar's breach — सन्धिच्छेदं कृत्वा गृहं प्रविष्टः.

questions.question: रात्रौ सुवर्णभाण्डं हस्ते गृहीत्वा कः सुप्तः आसीत्? (Who was asleep holding the golden casket?)
questions.answer: मैत्रेयः
questions.explanation: Maitreya slept holding the casket and, dreaming, handed it to the thief himself.

questions.question: चारुदत्तस्य पत्नी का? (Who is Charudatta's wife?)
questions.answer: धूता
questions.explanation: Dhuta is Charudatta's noble, self-sacrificing wife.

questions.question: What did Dhuta give to restore the value of the stolen deposit?
questions.answer: her precious रत्नावली (jewel necklace)
questions.explanation: Dhuta gave her own ratnavali so the deposit's value could be returned to Vasantasena.

questions.question: शर्विलकः किमर्थं चौर्यम् अकरोत्? (Why did Sharvilaka commit theft?)
questions.answer: to free Madanika from servitude
questions.explanation: He needed money for the दास्यमोचन (release from servitude) of his beloved Madanika.

questions.question: मदनिका का आसीत्? (Who was Madanika?)
questions.answer: वसन्तसेनायाः चेटी
questions.explanation: Madanika was Vasantasena's maid (चेटी), beloved of Sharvilaka.

questions.question: मैत्रेयः कः आसीत्? (Who was Maitreya?)
questions.answer: चारुदत्तस्य मित्रं विदूषकः
questions.explanation: Maitreya is Charudatta's devoted friend, the विदूषक of the play.

questions.question: At the end of the episode, what did Vasantasena do on learning the whole story?
options: She demanded double payment from Charudatta
questions.answer: She freed Madanika from servitude
questions.explanation: Understanding Sharvilaka's motive and Charudatta's innocence, she freed Madanika — दास्यात् मोचितवती.

questions.question: न्यासः इत्यस्य कः अर्थः? (What does 'nyasa' mean?)
options: a tax paid to the king
questions.answer: a deposit entrusted for safekeeping
questions.explanation: A न्यास (निक्षेप) is entrusted property that must be guarded and returned on demand.

questions.question: 'कष्टं न्यासस्य रक्षणम्' इत्यस्य वाक्यस्य कः भावः?
options: A deposit should never be accepted
questions.answer: Guarding a deposit is difficult
questions.explanation: The keeper bears heavy responsibility — hence 'hard indeed is the guarding of a deposit'.

questions.question: Why was the loss of the deposit especially dangerous for Charudatta?
options: Being poor, he feared people would believe he stole it himself
questions.answer: Being poor, he feared people would believe he stole it himself
questions.explanation: दरिद्रस्य मम वचनं कः श्रद्धास्यति? — a poor man's word is not trusted.

questions.question: न्यासस्य समानार्थकं पदं किम्? (A synonym of न्यास is:)
questions.answer: निक्षेपः
questions.explanation: न्यासः and निक्षेपः both mean a deposit held in trust.

questions.question: According to dharma, what must the keeper do if an accepted deposit is lost?
options: Nothing — the loss is the owner's fate
Restore its value from his own wealth
Report it to the king and forget it
questions.answer: Restore its value from his own wealth
questions.explanation: Charudatta restores the deposit's value with Dhuta's ratnavali — the dharma of restitution.

questions.question: 'कष्टं खलु न्यासस्य रक्षणम्' — एतत् वचनं कस्य? (Whose words are these?)
questions.answer: चारुदत्तस्य
questions.explanation: Charudatta utters this anguished line after the deposit is stolen.

questions.question: Why did Charudatta accept Vasantasena's deposit at all?
options: Protecting one who seeks refuge is the dharma of the good
questions.answer: Protecting one who seeks refuge is the dharma of the good
questions.explanation: शरणागतायाः रक्षणं सज्जनानां धर्मः — she came to his house for refuge and trusted him.

questions.question: What did Charudatta fear losing MOST after the theft?
options: his truth and character (सत्यं शीलं च)
questions.answer: his truth and character (सत्यं शीलं च)
questions.explanation: धनं नश्यतु नाम, मम सत्यं शीलं च न नश्येत् — let wealth perish, not truth and character.

questions.question: Which modern situation best parallels a न्यास as in the lesson?
options: Keeping a friend's valuables safe while she travels
questions.answer: Keeping a friend's valuables safe while she travels
questions.explanation: A deposit is property entrusted for safekeeping and return — exactly like holding a friend's valuables in trust.

questions.question: जात्या शर्विलकः कः आसीत्? (By birth, what was Sharvilaka?)
questions.answer: ब्राह्मणः
questions.explanation: Sharvilaka was a learned Brahmin youth — which makes his thieving a striking contradiction.

questions.question: How does Sharvilaka regard the act of burglary?
options: as a sin he performs carelessly
as a science/art with its own rules
as a joke to amuse Madanika
questions.answer: as a science/art with its own rules
questions.explanation: He examines the wall and cuts the breach methodically — चौर्यं शास्त्रम् इव मन्यते स्म.

questions.question: सन्धिच्छेदः इत्यस्य कः अर्थः?
options: cutting a breach in a wall to enter a house
questions.answer: cutting a breach in a wall to enter a house
questions.explanation: In this lesson सन्धिच्छेद is the burglar's opening cut in the house wall (not the grammar term सन्धिविच्छेद).

questions.question: शर्विलकः कस्याम् अनुरक्तः आसीत्? (With whom was Sharvilaka in love?)
questions.answer: मदनिकायाम्
questions.explanation: He loved Madanika, Vasantasena's maid, and stole to buy her freedom.

questions.question: The central contradiction in Sharvilaka's character is that:
options: he is rich yet steals for pleasure
he is a learned Brahmin yet practises theft
he hates Madanika yet frees her
he is a soldier yet fears the dark
questions.answer: he is a learned Brahmin yet practises theft
questions.explanation: Learning and dharma on one side, a गर्हित (despised) deed on the other — done for love.

questions.question: Why does Madanika tell Sharvilaka to return the ornaments to Vasantasena?
options: She wants to keep them herself
So that no blame (अपवादः) falls on the good Charudatta
questions.answer: So that no blame (अपवादः) falls on the good Charudatta
questions.explanation: सज्जनस्य अपवादः मा भूत् — she protects the honest man's name and corrects her lover's wrong.

questions.question: What does Sharvilaka's obedience to Madanika's counsel show?
options: that even a wrongdoer can turn back to dharma
questions.answer: that even a wrongdoer can turn back to dharma
questions.explanation: He returns the stolen ornaments — restitution as a return to righteousness.

questions.question: The night-theft scene, with its wall-breach and sleeping householders, chiefly illustrates:
options: the supernatural style of Sanskrit drama
the realism of ordinary life shown in a प्रकरण
questions.answer: the realism of ordinary life shown in a प्रकरण
questions.explanation: A burglar on stage, a ruined house, sleeping servants — everyday realism typical of Mricchakatika.

questions.question: The moment when sleeping Maitreya hands the casket to the thief is an example of:
questions.answer: dramatic irony
questions.explanation: The audience knows what Maitreya does not — the 'dream' hand-over gives the guarded deposit to the very thief.

questions.question: चारुदत्तः किमर्थं दरिद्रः अभवत्? (Why did Charudatta become poor?)
options: he gave away his wealth in charity
questions.answer: he gave away his wealth in charity
questions.explanation: दानशीलतया सर्वं धनं दत्त्वा दरिद्रः अभवत् — his generosity made him poor.

questions.question: On discovering the theft, Charudatta grieved chiefly for:
options: the broken trust and his imperilled good name
the damaged wall of his house
questions.answer: the broken trust and his imperilled good name
questions.explanation: His anguish is over विश्वास and यशः — not over wealth, which he never valued.

questions.question: धूतायाः आभरणस्य नाम किम्? (What was Dhuta's ornament called?)
questions.answer: रत्नावली
questions.explanation: Dhuta's precious jewel necklace, the ratnavali, replaced the stolen deposit's value.

questions.question: Dhuta's giving of her ratnavali best shows her:
options: spirit of sacrifice for honour and dharma
questions.answer: spirit of sacrifice for honour and dharma
questions.explanation: She gave her own precious स्त्रीधन quietly so the family's trust-debt could be repaid.

questions.question: What did Charudatta resolve after the theft?
options: to restore the deposit's value at any cost
to hide the matter from Vasantasena
questions.answer: to restore the deposit's value at any cost
questions.explanation: Though poor, he made restitution with the ratnavali — honesty over convenience.

questions.question: According to the lesson, Charudatta's TRUE wealth was:
questions.answer: his character (शीलम्) and honesty
questions.explanation: धनं नश्यतु नाम, मम सत्यं शीलं च न नश्येत् — character is the wealth he will not lose.

questions.question: In verse 2 (सत्यं न मे...), what 'burns' Charudatta the most?
options: the memory of his lost riches
that people grow cold in friendship toward a man who has lost wealth
the injustice of the king's court
questions.answer: that people grow cold in friendship toward a man who has lost wealth
questions.explanation: यत्सौहृदादपि जनाः शिथिलीभवन्ति — the cooling of friendship, not the loss itself, burns him.

questions.question: Which pair of values does the Charudatta-Dhuta household best exemplify?
questions.answer: honesty and sacrifice
questions.explanation: He insists on truth and restitution; she gives up her dearest possession for it.

questions.question: दारिद्र्यम् इत्यस्य कः अर्थः?
questions.answer: poverty
questions.explanation: दारिद्र्यम् = poverty; the central affliction of Charudatta's life.

questions.question: मरणम् इत्यस्य कः अर्थः?
questions.answer: death
questions.explanation: मरणम् = death; in the verse it is called अल्पक्लेशम् (of little pain).

questions.question: 'मम रोचते' इत्यत्र 'रोचते' इत्यस्य कः अर्थः?
questions.answer: pleases
questions.explanation: रुच् (आत्मनेपद) — रोचते = 'is pleasing to'; मम मरणं रोचते = death pleases me.

questions.question: अल्पक्लेशम् इत्यस्य कः अर्थः?
questions.answer: of little pain
questions.explanation: अल्प (little) + क्लेश (pain): death is a brief, one-time pain.

questions.question: अनन्तकम् इत्यस्य कः अर्थः?
questions.answer: endless
questions.explanation: अनन्तकम् = having no end; poverty is an endless sorrow (अनन्तकं दुःखम्).

questions.question: सौहृदम् इत्यस्य कः अर्थः?
questions.answer: friendship
questions.explanation: सौहृदम् (from सुहृद्, friend) = friendship, warm-heartedness.

questions.question: 'शिथिलीभवन्ति' इत्यस्य कः अर्थः?
questions.answer: become slack / grow cold
questions.explanation: शिथिल (loose) + भवन्ति: friendships loosen and cool toward the man who has lost wealth.

questions.question: विभवः इत्यस्य कः अर्थः?
questions.answer: wealth, prosperity
questions.explanation: विभवः = wealth; विभवनाशः = loss of wealth (विभवस्य नाशः).

questions.question: रक्षणम् इत्यस्य कः अर्थः?
questions.answer: protection, guarding
questions.explanation: रक्षणम् = guarding; न्यासस्य रक्षणम् = the guarding of a deposit.

questions.question: भाण्डम् इत्यस्य (सुवर्णभाण्डम् इत्यत्र) कः अर्थः?
questions.answer: a casket / vessel
questions.explanation: सुवर्णभाण्डम् = the golden casket in which the ornaments were kept.

questions.question: In verse 1, between poverty and death, Charudatta says he prefers:
options: death, because poverty is an endless sorrow
questions.answer: death, because poverty is an endless sorrow
questions.explanation: मरणं मम रोचते न दारिद्र्यम् — death is brief pain, poverty endless suffering.

questions.question: In verse 2, why is Charudatta NOT worried about the loss of wealth itself?
options: because riches come and go by the turns of fortune (भाग्यक्रमेण)
because he never had any wealth
questions.answer: because riches come and go by the turns of fortune (भाग्यक्रमेण)
questions.explanation: भाग्यक्रमेण हि धनानि भवन्ति यान्ति — wealth is fortune's toy, so its loss is no true grief.

questions.question: दारिद्र्यान्मरणात् इत्यस्य सन्धिविच्छेदः कः?
questions.answer: दारिद्र्यात् + मरणात्
questions.explanation: The final त् of दारिद्र्यात् becomes न् before म् (व्यञ्जनसन्धिः), as in तत् + मात्रम् = तन्मात्रम्.

questions.question: नास्ति इत्यस्य सन्धिविच्छेदः कः?
questions.answer: न + अस्ति
questions.explanation: अ + अ = आ (दीर्घसन्धिः): न + अस्ति = नास्ति.

questions.question: न्यासरक्षणम् इति कः समासः?
questions.answer: षष्ठीतत्पुरुषः
questions.explanation: विग्रहः: न्यासस्य रक्षणम् — the first member carries a genitive (षष्ठी) sense.

questions.question: नष्टधनः (= नष्टं धनं यस्य सः) इति कः समासः?
questions.answer: बहुव्रीहिः
questions.explanation: The compound names an outside person — 'one WHOSE wealth is lost' — hence बहुव्रीहि.

questions.question: चौरेण इति पदे का विभक्तिः?
questions.answer: तृतीया
questions.explanation: चौरेण = 'by the thief' — instrumental (तृतीया) singular.

questions.question: गृहे इति पदे का विभक्तिः?
questions.answer: सप्तमी
questions.explanation: गृहे = 'in the house' — locative (सप्तमी) singular.

questions.question: रक्षति इति क्रियापदं कस्मिन् लकारे अस्ति?
questions.answer: लट्
questions.explanation: रक्षति = 'guards' — present tense, लट् लकार.

questions.question: रक्षतु इति क्रियापदं कस्मिन् लकारे अस्ति?
questions.answer: लोट्
questions.explanation: रक्षतु = 'may he/she guard!' — imperative, लोट् लकार (as in एतान् अलङ्कारान् रक्षतु).

questions.question: श्रद्धास्यति इति क्रियापदं कस्मिन् लकारे अस्ति?
questions.answer: लृट्
questions.explanation: श्रद्धास्यति = 'will believe' — future tense, लृट् लकार (दरिद्रस्य मम वचनं कः श्रद्धास्यति?).

questions.question: दारिद्र्यात् इति पदे का विभक्तिः, कश्च तस्याः अर्थः अत्र?
questions.answer: पञ्चमी — 'than/from poverty'
questions.explanation: In दारिद्र्यान्मरणाद् वा the ablative (पञ्चमी) gives the sense of comparison/choice — 'than poverty or death'.

questions.question: Choose the correct translation: 'कष्टं खलु न्यासस्य रक्षणम्।'
options: A deposit is easy to guard.
Guarding a deposit is indeed difficult.
The deposit was guarded with difficulty.
One should never accept a deposit.
questions.answer: Guarding a deposit is indeed difficult.
questions.explanation: कष्टम् = difficult; खलु = indeed; न्यासस्य रक्षणम् = the guarding of a deposit.

questions.question: Choose the correct translation: 'अल्पक्लेशं मरणं दारिद्र्यमनन्तकं दुःखम्।'
options: Death is endless sorrow; poverty is brief pain.
Death is a brief pain; poverty is an endless sorrow.
Both death and poverty are brief pains.
Neither death nor poverty causes pain.
questions.answer: Death is a brief pain; poverty is an endless sorrow.
questions.explanation: अल्पक्लेशं मरणम् — death has little pain; दारिद्र्यम् अनन्तकं दुःखम् — poverty is endless sorrow.

questions.question: 'वसन्तसेना चारुदत्तस्य गृहे अलङ्कारान् स्थापयति' — इत्यस्य कः अर्थः?
options: Vasantasena sells ornaments in Charudatta's house.
Vasantasena places (her) ornaments in Charudatta's house.
Charudatta places ornaments in Vasantasena's house.
Vasantasena steals ornaments from Charudatta's house.
questions.answer: Vasantasena places (her) ornaments in Charudatta's house.
questions.explanation: स्थापयति = places/deposits; चारुदत्तस्य गृहे = in Charudatta's house.

questions.question: What is the purpose of writing the अन्वय of a verse?
options: to rearrange the verse words into natural prose order for easy understanding
to translate it into Hindi only
questions.answer: to rearrange the verse words into natural prose order for easy understanding
questions.explanation: अन्वय gives the prose word-order of a verse so its meaning becomes clear before translating.

questions.question: 'धूता स्वां रत्नावलीं पत्ये ददाति' — इत्यस्य कः अर्थः?
options: Dhuta gives her necklace to her husband.
Dhuta receives a necklace from her husband.
Dhuta hides her necklace from her husband.
Dhuta buys a necklace for her son.
questions.answer: Dhuta gives her necklace to her husband.
questions.explanation: स्वाम् = her own; पत्ये = to (her) husband (चतुर्थी); ददाति = gives.

questions.question: मृच्छकटिकम् is a नाटक whose hero is a legendary king.
questions.answer: False
questions.explanation: It is a प्रकरण — its plot is poet-invented and its hero, Charudatta, is an ordinary noble merchant-Brahmin.

questions.question: Tradition remembers Shudraka, the author of Mricchakatika, as a learned king.
questions.answer: True
questions.explanation: The play's prologue itself describes Shudraka as a learned राजा.

questions.question: Vasantasena deposited silver coins with Charudatta.
questions.answer: False
questions.explanation: She deposited her golden ornaments (सुवर्णालङ्काराः) kept in a golden casket.

questions.question: Sharvilaka committed the theft in order to free Madanika from servitude.
questions.answer: True
questions.explanation: He wanted money for the दास्यमोचन of his beloved Madanika, Vasantasena's maid.

questions.question: At the time of this episode Charudatta was a very wealthy merchant.
questions.answer: False
questions.explanation: He had become poor by giving away his wealth in charity; only his character remained rich.

questions.question: Dhuta gave her own ratnavali so that the deposit's value could be restored to Vasantasena.
questions.answer: True
questions.explanation: Her sacrifice of the precious necklace made the restitution possible.

questions.question: A न्यास is a gift that permanently becomes the property of the receiver.
questions.answer: False
questions.explanation: A न्यास is a deposit held in trust — it must be guarded and returned to the owner on demand.

questions.question: दारिद्र्यम् इत्यस्य अर्थः 'wealth' इति।
questions.answer: False
questions.explanation: दारिद्र्यम् means poverty, not wealth; wealth is धनम् / विभवः.

questions.question: रक्षतु इति क्रियापदं लोट्लकारे अस्ति।
questions.answer: True
questions.explanation: रक्षतु ('may he guard / please guard') is imperative — लोट् लकार.

questions.question: Charudatta grieved more for the broken trust than for the lost gold.
questions.answer: True
questions.explanation: He feared the loss of विश्वास and his good name; wealth, he said, may perish — not truth and character.

questions.question: मृच्छकटिकस्य रचयिता ________ अस्ति। (Fill in the author's name.)
questions.answer: शूद्रकः
questions.explanation: Mricchakatika was composed by Shudraka, traditionally a learned king.

questions.question: रूपकभेदेषु मृच्छकटिकम् ________ इति प्रकारस्य अस्ति। (Name the dramatic type.)
questions.answer: प्रकरणम्
questions.explanation: It is a प्रकरण — invented plot, ordinary noble hero, ten acts.

questions.question: कथायाः नगरी ________ अस्ति। (Name the city of the story.)
questions.answer: उज्जयिनी
questions.explanation: Charudatta and Vasantasena live in Ujjayini.

questions.question: वसन्तसेना ________ आसीत्। (गणिका / चेटी / राज्ञी — choose the correct word.)
questions.answer: गणिका
questions.explanation: Vasantasena was a wealthy, noble-hearted courtesan (गणिका) of Ujjayini.

questions.question: रक्षणार्थं स्थापितं धनं ________ इति कथ्यते। (What is entrusted property called?)
questions.answer: न्यासः
questions.explanation: Property entrusted for safekeeping is a न्यास (synonym: निक्षेपः).

questions.question: न्यासस्य चौर्यं ________ कृतवान्। (Who did the theft?)
questions.answer: शर्विलकः
questions.explanation: Sharvilaka stole the golden casket from Charudatta's house.

questions.question: चारुदत्तस्य मित्रं ________ नाम विदूषकः आसीत्।
questions.answer: मैत्रेयः
questions.explanation: Maitreya, the विदूषक, was Charudatta's devoted friend.

questions.question: चारुदत्तस्य पत्नी ________ आसीत्।
questions.answer: धूता
questions.explanation: Dhuta was Charudatta's noble wife, who gave her ratnavali for the restitution.

questions.question: धूता न्यासस्य स्थाने स्वां ________ दत्तवती। (Which ornament did she give?)
questions.answer: रत्नावलीम्
questions.explanation: She gave her precious jewel necklace, the रत्नावली, to restore the deposit's value.

questions.question: मदनिका वसन्तसेनायाः ________ आसीत्। (What was Madanika to Vasantasena?)
questions.answer: चेटी
questions.explanation: Madanika was Vasantasena's maid (चेटी / दासी), beloved of Sharvilaka.

questions.question: दारिद्र्यम् इत्यस्य आङ्ग्लभाषायाम् अर्थः ________ इति। (Give the English meaning.)
questions.answer: poverty
questions.explanation: दारिद्र्यम् = poverty — in the verse, an 'endless sorrow'.

questions.question: नास्ति = न + ________ । (Complete the सन्धिविच्छेद.)
questions.answer: अस्ति
questions.explanation: न + अस्ति = नास्ति (अ + अ = आ, दीर्घसन्धिः).

questions.question: 'न्यासस्य' इति पदे ________ विभक्तिः अस्ति। (Name the vibhakti.)
questions.answer: षष्ठी
questions.explanation: न्यासस्य = 'of the deposit' — genitive (षष्ठी) singular.

questions.question: 'रक्षिष्यति' इति क्रियापदं ________ लकारे अस्ति। (Name the lakara.)
questions.answer: लृट्
questions.explanation: रक्षिष्यति = 'will guard' — future tense, लृट् लकार.

questions.question: गृहप्रवेशाय भित्तौ छिद्रकरणं ________ इति उच्यते। (What is the burglar's wall-breach called?)
questions.answer: सन्धिच्छेदः
questions.explanation: Sharvilaka entered by सन्धिच्छेद — cutting a breach in the wall.

questions.question: Write a short note on the playwright शूद्रक and the meaning of the title मृच्छकटिकम्.
questions.answer: Shudraka is the author of मृच्छकटिकम्; tradition, following the play's own prologue, remembers him as a learned king versed in the Vedas, mathematics and elephant-lore. The title means 'The Little Clay Cart' (मृत् = clay + शकटिका = little cart), after the toy cart of Charudatta's small son — a touching symbol of the noble family's poverty.
questions.explanation: Author + title etymology + its symbolism.

questions.question: Distinguish a प्रकरण from a नाटक, giving मृच्छकटिकम् as an example.
questions.answer: In a नाटक the plot is taken from famous legend (Ramayana, Mahabharata) and the hero is a celebrated king or divine figure. In a प्रकरण the plot is invented by the poet (कविकल्पित), the hero is an ordinary noble citizen — a Brahmin, minister or merchant — and the heroine may be a गणिका. मृच्छकटिकम् is a प्रकरण: its hero Charudatta is a poor merchant-Brahmin of Ujjayini, its heroine Vasantasena is a courtesan, and its realistic invented plot brings thieves, servants and judges on stage in ten acts.
questions.explanation: Definition-contrast plus application to the play.

questions.question: Why did Vasantasena come to Charudatta's house, and what did she leave there?
questions.answer: Chased at night by wicked men, Vasantasena took refuge (शरणम्) in Charudatta's house. Trusting his famous honesty, she left her golden ornaments (in a golden casket) with him as a न्यास — a deposit for safekeeping — saying 'आर्य, एतान् अलङ्कारान् रक्षतु'.
questions.explanation: Refuge + trust + the deposit.

questions.question: Describe the scene in which the deposit passed from Maitreya's hands to the thief.
questions.answer: At night Maitreya slept holding the golden casket. When Sharvilaka entered through the wall-breach, the dreaming Maitreya, talking in his sleep, said 'take this golden casket' (गृहाण एतत् सुवर्णभाण्डम्) and placed it into the thief's very hands. Sharvilaka took it and slipped away — a moment of sharp dramatic irony.
questions.explanation: The sleep-talking hand-over — the audience knows what Maitreya does not.

questions.question: Name the six main characters of the episode and state each one's role in one line.
questions.answer: 1. चारुदत्तः — the poor, honest merchant-Brahmin who accepts the deposit. 2. वसन्तसेना — the noble गणिका who entrusts her ornaments. 3. मैत्रेयः — Charudatta's friend (विदूषक) who sleeps holding the casket. 4. शर्विलकः — the Brahmin thief who steals it for love. 5. मदनिका — Vasantasena's maid, Sharvilaka's beloved, who makes him return the ornaments. 6. धूता — Charudatta's wife, who gives her ratnavali for the restitution.
questions.explanation: Character-role recall across the whole episode.

questions.question: What is a न्यास? What duty does accepting one place on the keeper?
questions.answer: A न्यास (निक्षेप) is a deposit — valuables entrusted by one person to another for safekeeping, to be returned on demand. Accepting it is accepting a sacred trust: the keeper must guard it like his own life, and if it is lost while in his care, dharma requires him to make good its value from his own wealth.
questions.explanation: Definition + the dharma of guarding and restitution.

questions.question: Explain in your own words why the guarding of a deposit is called कष्ट (hard) in this lesson.
questions.answer: Guarding a deposit is hard because the keeper bears total responsibility with no reward: he must protect another's property like his own life, day and night. If it is stolen despite his care, he must still restore its value; and worse, suspicion falls on him — especially if he is poor, for people readily believe poverty drove him to take it himself. Charudatta suffers exactly this: the theft threatens his good name, and honesty compels him to give away even his household's last treasure. The burden of another's trust is heavier than one's own wealth.
questions.explanation: Responsibility + suspicion + cost of restitution.

questions.question: Quote (in Devanagari) Charudatta's words about wealth versus character after the theft, and translate them.
questions.answer: धनं नश्यतु नाम, मम सत्यं शीलं च न नश्येत्। — 'Let the wealth perish by all means, but let not my truth and my character perish.' He accepts the material loss but refuses to let the theft cost him his honesty and good name.
questions.explanation: The key sentence of Charudatta's resolve.

questions.question: Give two modern examples of a न्यास and state, for each, what the lesson teaches the keeper to do if it is lost.
questions.answer: Examples: (1) A neighbour leaves her jewellery box with you while her house is repaired; (2) a friend hands you his laptop or documents for safekeeping during travel. In both cases the keeper must guard the item like his own, and if it is lost or stolen despite his care, the lesson teaches him to inform the owner truthfully at once and to restore the value — repair, replace or repay — as Charudatta did with the ratnavali, because the owner's trust matters more than the keeper's money.
questions.explanation: Application of the dharma of restitution to daily life.

questions.question: In what sense does Sharvilaka treat theft 'like a science'? What does this detail add to the play?
questions.answer: Sharvilaka goes about the burglary methodically — he examines the wall, chooses the right spot and cuts a neat breach (सन्धिच्छेद), as though following the rules of a शास्त्र. The detail adds realism and irony: a trained Brahmin intellect is applied to a despised deed, sharpening the contradiction in his character and showing the प्रकरण's unusual willingness to stage ordinary and even criminal life.
questions.explanation: The 'scientific burglar' — realism plus character irony.

questions.question: How did Madanika react when Sharvilaka showed her the ornaments? What does her reaction reveal about her?
questions.answer: Madanika at once recognised the ornaments as her mistress Vasantasena's and was frightened. Learning they were stolen from the good Charudatta's house, she rebuked Sharvilaka and insisted the ornaments be returned so that no blame (अपवादः) should fall on the honest man. Her reaction reveals her loyalty to her mistress, her moral courage in correcting the man she loves, and her practical wisdom in finding the path of restitution.
questions.explanation: Recognition, rebuke, and the demand for return.

questions.question: Can Sharvilaka's theft be excused because his motive was love? Analyse both sides briefly.
questions.answer: For: his aim was noble in his own eyes — freeing Madanika from servitude, not personal greed; and he later undid the wrong by returning the ornaments, showing conscience. Against: a good motive does not purify a bad means; his theft endangered an innocent man — the poor Charudatta stood to lose his honour and be branded a thief — and a learned Brahmin knowingly chose अधर्म. The lesson's balance: the deed remains wrong, but his restitution shows that the door back to dharma is always open.
questions.explanation: Motive vs means; the harm to Charudatta; restitution as partial redemption.

questions.question: How did Charudatta become poor, and why did the city still honour him?
questions.answer: Charudatta became poor through his own generosity — दानशीलतया he gave away his great wealth to all who asked. The city still honoured him because his character (शीलम्) and courtesy (सौजन्यम्) were unblemished: people trusted him so completely that even a wealthy stranger like Vasantasena chose his house for her deposit.
questions.explanation: Poverty by charity; honour by character.

questions.question: 'धूता is as much a hero of this episode as चारुदत्तः.' Do you agree? Justify.
questions.answer: Yes. Charudatta's honesty resolves that the deposit must be restored, but it is Dhuta who makes the restitution possible: she gives up her own precious ratnavali — perhaps the family's last treasure and her personal स्त्रीधन — quietly and at once, asking for nothing. Her sacrifice involves real loss, made without public credit, purely for dharma and the family's honour. Heroism here lies in giving, and by that measure Dhuta's deed equals, even crowns, her husband's resolve.
questions.explanation: Evaluative judgement on Dhuta's quiet sacrifice.

questions.question: What does the episode suggest is 'true wealth'? Answer with evidence from the text.
questions.answer: True wealth is character, not gold. Charudatta, having lost all money, still commands the city's trust (Vasantasena deposits her ornaments with him); after the theft he says 'let wealth perish, but not my truth and character' (धनं नश्यतु नाम, मम सत्यं शीलं च न नश्येत्); and the family willingly spends its last treasure to keep its honesty intact. Gold comes and goes भाग्यक्रमेण, but शीलम् is one's own.
questions.explanation: Character as wealth, evidenced by trust, the resolve, and the ratnavali.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ of: अनुधाविता, शरणम्, स्वप्नायमानः, अपहृतः, वृत्तान्तः.
questions.answer: अनुधाविता = chased, pursued; शरणम् = refuge, shelter; स्वप्नायमानः = dreaming, talking in sleep; अपहृतः = stolen, carried off; वृत्तान्तः = account, the whole story.
questions.explanation: Vocabulary from the prose passages.

questions.question: Write the अन्वय of: दारिद्र्यान्मरणाद् वा मरणं मम रोचते न दारिद्र्यम् । अल्पक्लेशं मरणं दारिद्र्यमनन्तकं दुःखम् ॥ and give its meaning.
questions.answer: अन्वयः: दारिद्र्यात् मरणात् वा (मध्ये) मम मरणं रोचते, न दारिद्र्यम्; मरणम् अल्पक्लेशम्, दारिद्र्यम् (तु) अनन्तकं दुःखम्। Meaning: Between poverty and death, death pleases me, not poverty; for death is a pain of a moment, while poverty is a sorrow without end.
questions.explanation: Prose order of the verse plus translation.

questions.question: Explain the meaning of the verse सत्यं न मे विभवनाशकृतास्ति चिन्ता... What truth about society does it state?
questions.answer: Charudatta says: truly, I have no anxiety over the loss of wealth itself, for riches come and go by the turns of fortune (भाग्यक्रमेण). What burns him is that when a man's wealth is gone, people grow slack even in friendship (सौहृदादपि जनाः शिथिलीभवन्ति). The verse states a bitter social truth: much of the world's warmth follows wealth; the poor man loses not only money but respect, trust and friends — and that loss, not the gold, is poverty's real wound.
questions.explanation: The verse's bhava: fortunes are fickle, and so — sadly — are friends.

questions.question: Do the सन्धिविच्छेद and name the sandhi: (a) मृच्छकटिकम् (b) यत्सौहृदात्.
questions.answer: (a) मृच्छकटिकम् = मृत् + शकटिका — त् + श् becomes च्छ् (श्चुत्वसन्धिः/व्यञ्जनसन्धिः). (b) यत्सौहृदात् = यत् + सौहृदात् — simple consonant joining of त् with स् (व्यञ्जनसन्धिः, no change of form).
questions.explanation: Both occur in the lesson: the play's title and verse 2.

questions.question: Identify the samasa and give the विग्रह: (a) दारिद्र्यपीडितः (b) ब्राह्मणयुवकः (c) सुवर्णभाण्डम्.
questions.answer: (a) दारिद्र्यपीडितः = दारिद्र्येण पीडितः — तृतीयातत्पुरुषः (afflicted BY poverty). (b) ब्राह्मणयुवकः = ब्राह्मणः (चासौ) युवकः — कर्मधारयः (a youth who is a Brahmin). (c) सुवर्णभाण्डम् = सुवर्णस्य भाण्डम् — षष्ठीतत्पुरुषः (casket OF gold).
questions.explanation: Three compounds from the lesson with case-relations त्रितीया, sameness, षष्ठी.

questions.question: Translate into English: 'प्रातःकाले चारुदत्तः न्यासस्य अपहरणं ज्ञात्वा अतीव व्यथितः अभवत्।'
questions.answer: In the morning, having learnt of the theft of the deposit, Charudatta became deeply pained/anguished. (प्रातःकाले = in the morning; अपहरणं ज्ञात्वा = having come to know of the stealing; अतीव व्यथितः = extremely distressed.)
questions.explanation: Prose translation with the gerund ज्ञात्वा = 'having known'.

questions.question: Translate into Sanskrit: (a) 'Guarding a deposit is difficult.' (b) 'Vasantasena freed Madanika.'
questions.answer: (a) कष्टं न्यासस्य रक्षणम् (अस्ति)। (b) वसन्तसेना मदनिकां (दास्यात्) अमोचयत् / मोचितवती।
questions.explanation: Sentence (a) is the title itself; (b) uses मुच् in past tense with द्वितीया object.

questions.question: Write an essay on शूद्रक's मृच्छकटिकम् — its author, title, dramatic type, setting, main characters and the qualities that make it one of the most loved Sanskrit plays.
questions.answer: मृच्छकटिकम् ('The Little Clay Cart', from मृत् + शकटिका) is a ten-act play by Shudraka, whom its own prologue describes as a learned king versed in the Vedas, mathematics and elephant-lore. It is a प्रकरण — the plot is the poet's invention, the hero an ordinary noble citizen — and it is set in the bustling city of Ujjayini. Its hero Charudatta is a Brahmin merchant impoverished by his own generosity; the heroine Vasantasena is a wealthy, noble-hearted गणिका who loves him for his virtue. Around them move Maitreya the loyal विदूषक, the wife Dhuta, the Brahmin-thief Sharvilaka and the maid Madanika. The play is loved for its realism — poor households, burglars at work, gamblers, servants and law-courts appear on stage; for its humane characters, in whom nobility appears in courtesans and thieves as well as in Brahmins; for its gentle humour and pathos; and for its moral vision, summed up in the deposit episode, that character outshines wealth. The toy clay cart of Charudatta's son, which gives the play its name, is its perfect symbol: poverty on the outside, love and dignity within.
questions.explanation: Author, title-meaning, type, setting, characters, and reasons for the play's fame.

questions.question: Narrate in detail the story of कष्टं न्यासस्य रक्षणम् from the deposit to the final restitution, bringing out the sequence of events clearly.
questions.answer: In Ujjayini lived Charudatta, a Brahmin merchant made poor by his boundless charity, with his wife Dhuta and friend Maitreya. One night the courtesan Vasantasena, chased by wicked men, took refuge in his house and, trusting his famed honesty, left her golden ornaments with him as a न्यास. Some nights later Sharvilaka — a learned Brahmin who had turned to theft to buy the freedom of his beloved Madanika, Vasantasena's maid — cut a breach in the wall (सन्धिच्छेद) of the old house and crept in. Maitreya lay asleep with the golden casket in his hand; dreaming, he muttered 'take this golden casket' and handed it to the thief, who escaped. At dawn Charudatta discovered the loss and was shattered — not for the gold, but because a poor man's word would not be believed and the trust placed in him lay broken: कष्टं खलु न्यासस्य रक्षणम्. Dhuta then gave her own precious ratnavali so that the deposit's value could be restored, and Maitreya carried it to Vasantasena. Meanwhile Madanika recognised her mistress's ornaments, rebuked Sharvilaka, and made him return them to Vasantasena so no blame would touch the good Charudatta. Learning the whole story, Vasantasena freed Madanika from servitude. Honesty was vindicated, the trust repaid, and truth triumphed in the end.
questions.explanation: Complete narrative arc: deposit → theft → anguish → ratnavali → return → freedom.

questions.question: 'कष्टं न्यासस्य रक्षणम्' — explain the full meaning of this statement in the context of the lesson, and discuss its relevance for public and private life today.
questions.answer: The statement means 'hard indeed is the guarding of a deposit'. In the lesson it is Charudatta's cry when Vasantasena's entrusted ornaments are stolen from his house. Its layers: (1) A deposit must be guarded like one's own life, day and night — a ceaseless burden. (2) If it is lost, the keeper must restore its value even from his last wealth, as Charudatta did with Dhuta's ratnavali. (3) Worst of all, suspicion falls on the keeper — a poor man especially will be accused of taking it himself; so the deposit endangers the keeper's most precious possession, his good name. Relevance today: every position of trust is a न्यास — a bank holding deposits, an official managing public money, a trustee of an orphan's property, a friend keeping another's valuables, even a leader entrusted with people's hopes. The lesson teaches that such trust must be carried with total honesty; that loss must be met with truthful disclosure and restitution, not concealment; and that the burden of trust, though heavy (कष्ट), is the very measure of a person's nobility. Those who guard trust at personal cost, like Charudatta, are society's real wealth.
questions.explanation: Three layers of the burden + modern applications of trusteeship.

questions.question: Draw a character sketch of शर्विलक, analysing the contradictions in his personality and his journey within the episode.
questions.answer: Sharvilaka is one of Sanskrit drama's most striking creations — a bundle of contradictions. By birth and training he is a learned Brahmin, yet he practises burglary; and he practises it not crudely but as a शास्त्र, examining the wall and cutting his breach with a craftsman's method. His motive is neither greed nor malice but love: he needs money to free Madanika, Vasantasena's maid, from servitude. Thus a noble end drives him to an ignoble means. His intellect is real, his courage is real, and — as events prove — his conscience is real too. When Madanika recognises the stolen ornaments and rebukes him, he does not argue or flee: he accepts her counsel, returns the ornaments to Vasantasena, and lifts the shadow of blame from the innocent Charudatta. His journey within the episode is therefore a small moral arc — from अधर्म committed for love, to restitution chosen for dharma. Shudraka uses him to teach two things: that learning without conduct can stumble, and that no one who turns back to righteousness is beyond redemption.
questions.explanation: Learning vs deed, love as motive, method, conscience, and the arc to restitution.

questions.question: Draw a character sketch of चारुदत्त as revealed in this episode, and evaluate the part played by धूता in upholding the family's honour.
questions.answer: Charudatta is nobility in poverty. Once very rich, he has given his wealth away in charity; what remains is his शीलम् — a character so trusted that Vasantasena chooses his house for her deposit. He accepts the न्यास as the dharma owed to one who seeks refuge. When it is stolen, his grief shows his scale of values: he mourns not the gold but the broken trust and his imperilled good name — 'who will believe a poor man?' — and resolves at once that the deposit's value must be restored: धनं नश्यतु नाम, मम सत्यं शीलं च न नश्येत्. His two verses reveal a sensitive man for whom poverty's true sting is the cooling of friendship, and death itself is lighter than dishonour. Dhuta is his equal in this nobility. Without being asked, she gives her own precious ratnavali — likely her स्त्रीधन and the family's last treasure — so that restitution can be made. Her sacrifice is quiet, immediate and complete; she seeks no credit and counts the family's honour above her dearest ornament. If Charudatta supplies the resolve, Dhuta supplies the means: between them the episode shows a household in which honesty is not one person's virtue but the family's shared wealth.
questions.explanation: Charudatta: trust, grief for honour, resolve; Dhuta: silent decisive sacrifice.

questions.question: Write the two verses of Charudatta given in the lesson with their अन्वय and meanings, and explain what together they tell us about the experience of poverty.
questions.answer: Verse 1: दारिद्र्यान्मरणाद् वा मरणं मम रोचते न दारिद्र्यम् । अल्पक्लेशं मरणं दारिद्र्यमनन्तकं दुःखम् ॥ अन्वयः: दारिद्र्यात् मरणात् वा मम मरणं रोचते, न दारिद्र्यम्; मरणम् अल्पक्लेशम्, दारिद्र्यम् अनन्तकं दुःखम्। Meaning: between poverty and death I would choose death — death is a brief pain, poverty an endless sorrow. Verse 2: सत्यं न मे विभवनाशकृतास्ति चिन्ता भाग्यक्रमेण हि धनानि भवन्ति यान्ति । एतत्तु मां दहति नष्टधनाश्रयस्य यत्सौहृदादपि जनाः शिथिलीभवन्ति ॥ अन्वयः: सत्यं मे विभवनाशकृता चिन्ता न अस्ति, हि धनानि भाग्यक्रमेण भवन्ति यान्ति; तु एतत् मां दहति यत् नष्टधनाश्रयस्य जनाः सौहृदात् अपि शिथिलीभवन्ति। Meaning: I have no worry over lost wealth, for riches come and go by fortune's turns; what burns me is that people grow cold even in friendship toward a man whose wealth is gone. Together the verses say that poverty's real torment is not hunger for comforts but unending social pain: daily humiliation, the inability to give, suspicion, and the withering of friendships. Material loss is fate's play and can be borne; the loss of trust, respect and warmth is the wound that never closes — which is why the generous, self-respecting Charudatta calls poverty a sorrow worse than death.
questions.explanation: Both verses with anvaya + the combined message about poverty's social wound.

questions.question: From the lesson, write (a) two sandhi examples with विच्छेद and names, (b) three samasa examples with विग्रह and names, and (c) one verb form each in लट्, लृट् and लोट् with meanings.
questions.answer: (a) सन्धिः: दारिद्र्यान्मरणात् = दारिद्र्यात् + मरणात् — त् becomes न् before म् (व्यञ्जनसन्धिः); नास्ति = न + अस्ति — अ + अ = आ (दीर्घसन्धिः). (Also: मृच्छकटिकम् = मृत् + शकटिका, श्चुत्वसन्धिः.) (b) समासः: न्यासरक्षणम् = न्यासस्य रक्षणम् (षष्ठीतत्पुरुषः); दारिद्र्यपीडितः = दारिद्र्येण पीडितः (तृतीयातत्पुरुषः); नष्टधनः = नष्टं धनं यस्य सः (बहुव्रीहिः). (c) लकाराः: रक्षति — 'guards' (लट्, present); रक्षिष्यति / श्रद्धास्यति — 'will guard / will believe' (लृट्, future); रक्षतु / प्रत्यर्पय — 'may (he) guard! / return (it)!' (लोट्, imperative).
questions.explanation: Consolidated grammar answer covering sandhi, samasa and lakara from the text.

questions.question: Write five simple Sanskrit sentences (in Devanagari) summarising the story of the lesson, and give the English meaning of each. Then state, in two or three English sentences, the message you would take from this lesson for your own life.
questions.answer: 1. वसन्तसेना चारुदत्तस्य गृहे स्वालङ्कारान् न्यासरूपेण स्थापितवती। (Vasantasena placed her ornaments in Charudatta's house as a deposit.) 2. रात्रौ शर्विलकः सन्धिच्छेदं कृत्वा तं न्यासम् अचोरयत्। (At night Sharvilaka cut a breach and stole that deposit.) 3. चारुदत्तः धनस्य नाशात् अपि विश्वासस्य नाशं अधिकं शोचति स्म। (Charudatta grieved more over the loss of trust than the loss of wealth.) 4. धूता स्वां रत्नावलीं न्यासस्य स्थाने दत्तवती। (Dhuta gave her own necklace in place of the deposit.) 5. अन्ते सत्यं शीलं च विजयेते। (In the end truth and character triumph.) Message: When someone trusts me with anything — money, a possession, a secret or a duty — I must guard it with full care and, if it is ever lost, own the truth and make it good at my own cost. Honesty kept in hardship, like Charudatta's, is worth more than any wealth.
questions.explanation: Original composition in simple Sanskrit plus a personal application of the moral.

questions.question:
अधोलिखितं गद्यांशं पठित्वा प्रश्नान् उत्तरत —
'मृच्छकटिकं नाम प्रकरणं शूद्रकेण विरचितम्। अस्मिन् रूपके दश अङ्काः सन्ति। कथा उज्जयिन्यां नगर्यां प्रचलति। अस्य नायकः चारुदत्तः न राजा, किन्तु सामान्यः सज्जनः ब्राह्मणवणिक् अस्ति; नायिका च वसन्तसेना गणिका।'
(a) मृच्छकटिकं केन विरचितम्? कति अङ्काः तस्मिन् सन्ति? (b) कथा कस्यां नगर्यां प्रचलति? (c) From the passage, state two features that make this play a प्रकरण rather than a नाटक. (d) Explain the meaning of the title मृच्छकटिकम् and what it symbolises.
questions.answer: (a) मृच्छकटिकं शूद्रकेण विरचितम्; तस्मिन् दश अङ्काः सन्ति (ten acts). (b) कथा उज्जयिन्यां नगर्यां प्रचलति — the story unfolds in Ujjayini. (c) Two प्रकरण features from the passage: the hero is an ordinary noble citizen (a Brahmin merchant, not a king or god), and the heroine may be a गणिका (courtesan) — also, the plot is the poet's own invention (कविकल्पित), not taken from epic. (d) मृच्छकटिकम् = मृत् (clay) + शकटिका (little cart), 'The Little Clay Cart' — the toy cart of Charudatta's little son, a touching symbol of the family's poverty on the outside and its love and dignity within.
questions.explanation: Tests recognition of the play's authorship, structure, setting and the defining features of the प्रकरण type from a seen-style passage.

questions.question:
अधोलिखितं गद्यांशं पठित्वा प्रश्नान् उत्तरत —
'एकदा रात्रौ वसन्तसेना नाम गणिका दुर्जनैः अनुधाविता चारुदत्तस्य गृहं शरणं प्रविष्टा। सा तस्य सज्जनतायां विश्वासं कृत्वा स्वकीयान् सुवर्णालङ्कारान् न्यासरूपेण तस्य हस्ते स्थापितवती। शरणागतायाः रक्षणं सज्जनानां धर्मः इति मत्वा चारुदत्तः तं न्यासं स्वीकृतवान्।'
(a) वसन्तसेना कैः अनुधाविता चारुदत्तस्य गृहं प्रविष्टा? (b) सा किं न्यासरूपेण स्थापितवती? (c) 'अनुधाविता' इति पदस्य कः अर्थः? (d) Translate: 'शरणागतायाः रक्षणं सज्जनानां धर्मः इति मत्वा चारुदत्तः तं न्यासं स्वीकृतवान्।'
questions.answer: (a) वसन्तसेना दुर्जनैः अनुधाविता (chased by wicked men) चारुदत्तस्य गृहं शरणं प्रविष्टा. (b) सा स्वकीयान् सुवर्णालङ्कारान् (her own golden ornaments) न्यासरूपेण चारुदत्तस्य हस्ते स्थापितवती. (c) अनुधाविता = chased, pursued. (d) 'Thinking that protecting one who has come for refuge is the dharma of the good, Charudatta accepted that deposit.'
questions.explanation: Comprehension of the entrustment scene — who, what, why — with a word-meaning and a translation, following the lesson's own retelling.

questions.question:
अधोलिखितं गद्यांशं पठित्वा प्रश्नान् उत्तरत —
'अन्यस्यां रात्रौ शर्विलकः नाम ब्राह्मणयुवकः चौर्यार्थं चारुदत्तस्य जीर्णं गृहम् आगतवान्। सः मदनिकायाम् अनुरक्तः आसीत्; तस्याः दास्यमोचनाय धनम् ऐच्छत्। सः चौर्यं शास्त्रम् इव मन्यते स्म — भित्तेः परीक्षां कृत्वा सन्धिच्छेदं कृत्वा च गृहं प्रविष्टः।'
(a) शर्विलकः किमर्थं धनम् ऐच्छत्? (b) सः गृहं कथं प्रविष्टः? (c) What is meant by सन्धिच्छेदः? (d) Analyse the contradiction in Sharvilaka's character shown in this passage — what does 'चौर्यं शास्त्रम् इव मन्यते स्म' reveal about him?
questions.answer: (a) सः मदनिकायाः दास्यमोचनाय (to buy his beloved Madanika's freedom from servitude) धनम् ऐच्छत्. (b) भित्तेः परीक्षां कृत्वा सन्धिच्छेदं कृत्वा च — after examining the wall and cutting a breach, he entered. (c) सन्धिच्छेदः = the burglar's breach — cutting an opening in the wall of a house to enter it. (d) The contradiction: he is a ब्राह्मणयुवकः, a learned Brahmin who should live by dharma, yet he practises theft; and he treats theft as a 'science' (शास्त्रम् इव) — testing the wall methodically like a scholar. His motive is love, not greed, so he is neither a pure villain nor a good man: a learned mind misapplied, which is why Madanika can later turn him back to the right path.
questions.explanation: The passage exposes Sharvilaka's paradox — Brahmin learning applied to burglary for love — which the student must analyse, not merely recall.

questions.question:
अधोलिखितं गद्यांशं पठित्वा प्रश्नान् उत्तरत —
'प्रातःकाले चारुदत्तः न्यासस्य अपहरणं ज्ञात्वा अतीव व्यथितः अभवत् — हा कष्टम्! दरिद्रस्य मम वचनं कः श्रद्धास्यति? जनाः वदिष्यन्ति — दारिद्र्यपीडितः चारुदत्तः एव न्यासम् अपहृतवान् इति। धनं नश्यतु नाम, मम सत्यं शीलं च न नश्येत्।'
(a) चारुदत्तः किं ज्ञात्वा व्यथितः अभवत्? (b) जनाः किं वदिष्यन्ति इति सः अशङ्कत? (c) What, according to his last sentence, does Charudatta value more than wealth? (d) Evaluate: was Charudatta's fear 'दरिद्रस्य मम वचनं कः श्रद्धास्यति?' justified? What does this scene show about the position of a poor but honest man in society?
questions.answer: (a) वसन्तसेनायाः न्यासस्य अपहरणं (the theft of Vasantasena's deposit from his house) ज्ञात्वा सः व्यथितः अभवत्. (b) 'दारिद्र्यपीडितः चारुदत्तः एव न्यासम् अपहृतवान्' इति — people would say that poverty-stricken Charudatta himself took the deposit. (c) His truth and character — 'धनं नश्यतु नाम, मम सत्यं शीलं च न नश्येत्': let wealth perish, but not his सत्य and शील. (d) Yes, the fear was justified: the world judges by circumstances, and a poor custodian of lost valuables is the first suspect — his word carries no weight of wealth behind it. The scene shows that for the poor, reputation is fragile and trust is their only capital; hence Charudatta grieves for lost विश्वास, not lost gold, and resolves on restitution to protect his character, proving that true wealth is शील.
questions.explanation: Evaluation of Charudatta's anguish speech — the heart of the lesson's title कष्टं न्यासस्य रक्षणम् — and of society's treatment of the honest poor.

questions.question:
अधोलिखितं श्लोकं पठित्वा प्रश्नान् उत्तरत —
'दारिद्र्यान्मरणाद् वा मरणं मम रोचते न दारिद्र्यम्।
अल्पक्लेशं मरणं दारिद्र्यमनन्तकं दुःखम्॥'
(a) कस्य अयं श्लोकः? मरणं दारिद्र्यं वा — किं तस्मै रोचते? (b) मरणं कीदृशम्? दारिद्र्यं च कीदृशम्? (c) कुरुत सन्धिविच्छेदम् — 'दारिद्र्यान्मरणात्'। (d) Analyse why the speaker calls poverty an 'endless sorrow' while death is only a 'brief pain'.
questions.answer: (a) अयं श्लोकः चारुदत्तस्य (from Mricchakatika, Act 1). तस्मै मरणं रोचते, न दारिद्र्यम् — between the two, death pleases him, not poverty. (b) मरणम् अल्पक्लेशम् (of little/brief pain); दारिद्र्यम् अनन्तकं दुःखम् (an endless sorrow). (c) दारिद्र्यान्मरणात् = दारिद्र्यात् + मरणात् — the त् of दारिद्र्यात् becomes न् before म् (व्यञ्जनसन्धिः). (d) Death hurts only once and is over; poverty is a living, daily humiliation for a self-respecting and generous man — he must endure disrespect, suspicion and the inability to give, every day without end. Hence for Charudatta poverty, not death, is the greater suffering.
questions.explanation: Verse-based case: recall of the first famous verse, its epithets, a sandhi split taught in the lesson's grammar section, and analysis of its भाव.

questions.question:
अधोलिखितं श्लोकं पठित्वा प्रश्नान् उत्तरत —
'सत्यं न मे विभवनाशकृतास्ति चिन्ता भाग्यक्रमेण हि धनानि भवन्ति यान्ति।
एतत्तु मां दहति नष्टधनाश्रयस्य यत्सौहृदादपि जनाः शिथिलीभवन्ति॥'
(a) किं चारुदत्तं न चिन्तयति? (What does he say he does NOT worry about?) (b) किं तं दहति? (c) 'शिथिलीभवन्ति' इति पदस्य कः अर्थः? Give the अन्वय of the second line. (d) Translate the whole verse into simple English and state its central idea in one sentence.
questions.answer: (a) विभवनाशकृता चिन्ता तं न बाधते — he has no worry caused by the loss of wealth, for riches come and go by the turns of fortune (भाग्यक्रमेण धनानि भवन्ति यान्ति). (b) एतत् तं दहति यत् नष्टधनस्य जनस्य सौहृदात् अपि जनाः शिथिलीभवन्ति — what burns him is that people grow cold even in friendship toward a man whose wealth is gone. (c) शिथिलीभवन्ति = become slack, grow loose/cold. अन्वयः: तु एतत् मां दहति यत् नष्टधनाश्रयस्य (जनस्य) सौहृदात् अपि जनाः शिथिलीभवन्ति। (d) Translation: 'Truly I have no anxiety caused by the loss of wealth — riches come and go by the turns of fortune. But this burns me: that when a man's wealth is lost, people grow cold even in friendship.' Central idea: Charudatta's real pain is not lost gold but the loss of human warmth and trust that poverty brings.
questions.explanation: Tests the second verse with अन्वय and translation — the NYA-08 skills — plus grasp of its central idea.

questions.question:
अधोलिखितं गद्यांशं पठित्वा प्रश्नान् उत्तरत —
'तदा धूता स्वस्य बहुमूल्यां रत्नावलीं आनीय पत्युः समीपं प्रेषितवती — इयं रत्नावली न्यासस्य स्थाने वसन्तसेनायै दीयताम् इति। भार्यायाः त्यागं दृष्ट्वा चारुदत्तः गद्गदः अभवत्। एवं दरिद्रः अपि सः न्यासस्य मूल्यं प्रत्यर्पितवान्।'
(a) धूता किं प्रेषितवती? किमर्थम्? (b) 'गद्गदः' इति पदस्य कः अर्थः? (c) Translate: 'एवं दरिद्रः अपि सः न्यासस्य मूल्यं प्रत्यर्पितवान्।' (d) Evaluate Dhuta's act: what does her willing sacrifice of her own ratnavali show about her character and about the dharma of a householder toward a न्यास?
questions.answer: (a) धूता स्वस्य बहुमूल्यां रत्नावलीं प्रेषितवती — she sent her own precious jewel-necklace, so that it could be given to Vasantasena in place of the stolen deposit (न्यासस्य स्थाने). (b) गद्गदः = choked with emotion, voice broken by feeling. (c) 'Thus, though poor, he returned (made good) the value of the deposit.' (d) Dhuta's act shows quiet, unasked-for nobility: she gives her last precious ornament, her स्त्रीधन, without complaint, to protect her husband's honour and the sanctity of the trust. It shows that the dharma of guarding a न्यास binds the whole household — if the deposit is lost, it must be made good from one's own wealth — and that Dhuta equals Charudatta in शील: the family's real रत्नावली is its character.
questions.explanation: The restitution scene: comprehension plus an evaluation of Dhuta's sacrifice as the lesson's model of householder dharma toward a trust.

questions.question:
अधोलिखितं गद्यांशं पठित्वा प्रश्नान् उत्तरत —
'शर्विलकः तान् अलङ्कारान् मदनिकायै दर्शितवान्। सा स्वस्वामिन्याः अलङ्कारान् परिचित्य भीता अभवत् — एते वसन्तसेनायाः अलङ्काराः! त्वं सज्जनस्य चारुदत्तस्य गृहात् एतान् अपहृतवान्। तस्य अपवादः मा भूत्। एतान् वसन्तसेनायै प्रत्यर्पय इति। शर्विलकः तथा एव कृतवान्।'
(a) मदनिका अलङ्कारान् परिचित्य किमर्थं भीता अभवत्? (b) सा शर्विलकं किं कर्तुम् आदिष्टवती? (c) 'अपवादः' इति पदस्य कः अर्थः? (d) Analyse Madanika's role in this scene: how does she turn a theft into a restitution, and what does the episode's outcome (Vasantasena freeing her) suggest about the play's moral vision?
questions.answer: (a) यतः ते अलङ्काराः तस्याः स्वामिन्याः वसन्तसेनायाः आसन्, ते च सज्जनस्य चारुदत्तस्य गृहात् अपहृताः — she recognised her mistress's ornaments and realised her beloved had robbed the good Charudatta. (b) 'एतान् वसन्तसेनायै प्रत्यर्पय' — return these ornaments to Vasantasena, so that no blame falls on Charudatta (तस्य अपवादः मा भूत्). (c) अपवादः = blame, ill-repute, false accusation. (d) Madanika is the thief's conscience: instead of enjoying stolen wealth meant to free her, she puts Charudatta's good name above her own freedom and commands restitution — and Sharvilaka obeys, showing his core is still noble. Vasantasena, learning the whole story, frees Madanika anyway: the play's moral vision is that even a thief and a maid can act with dharma, and honesty is rewarded — सत्यं शीलं च अन्ते विजयते.
questions.explanation: Analysis of Madanika as the agent who reverses the theft, and of the episode's ending as the play's statement that character exists at every social level.

questions.question:
अधोलिखितं वाक्यद्वयं पठित्वा व्याकरणप्रश्नान् उत्तरत —
'शर्विलकः सन्धिच्छेदं कृत्वा सुवर्णभाण्डम् अपहृतवान्। दारिद्र्यपीडितः चारुदत्तः वसन्तसेनायै न्यासस्य मूल्यं प्रत्यर्पितवान्।'
(a) कुरुत सन्धिविच्छेदम् — 'मृच्छकटिकम्'; कः सन्धिः? (b) 'सुवर्णभाण्डम्' तथा 'दारिद्र्यपीडितः' इत्यनयोः समासविग्रहं कृत्वा समासनाम लिखत। (c) 'वसन्तसेनायै' तथा 'गृहात्' — का विभक्तिः? (state the vibhakti and its sense). (d) 'प्रत्यर्पय', 'श्रद्धास्यति', 'रक्षति' — एषु कः लकारः? (identify the लकार of each form).
questions.answer: (a) मृच्छकटिकम् = मृत् + शकटिका — त् + श् becomes च्छ् (श्चुत्वसन्धिः, a व्यञ्जनसन्धि). (b) सुवर्णभाण्डम् = सुवर्णस्य भाण्डम् — षष्ठीतत्पुरुषः; दारिद्र्यपीडितः = दारिद्र्येण पीडितः — तृतीयातत्पुरुषः. (c) वसन्तसेनायै — चतुर्थी विभक्तिः (dative: 'for/to Vasantasena'); गृहात् — पञ्चमी विभक्तिः (ablative: 'from the house'). (d) प्रत्यर्पय — लोट् लकारः (command: 'return!'); श्रद्धास्यति — लृट् लकारः (future: 'will believe'); रक्षति — लट् लकारः (present: 'guards').
questions.explanation: A grammar case built entirely on forms taught in the lesson: श्चुत्व sandhi of the title, two tatpurusha compounds, two vibhaktis and three lakāras.

questions.question:
अधोलिखितं वाक्यं पठित्वा प्रश्नान् उत्तरत —
'कष्टं खलु न्यासस्य रक्षणम्! न्यासः विश्वासस्य धनम् — यः न्यासं स्वीकरोति सः तं प्राणवत् रक्षेत्, नष्टे च सति स्वधनेन तस्य मूल्यं प्रत्यर्पयेत्।'
(a) कः न्यासः? (Define न्यास in one or two sentences; give its other Sanskrit name.) (b) यः न्यासं स्वीकरोति तस्य कौ धर्मौ अत्र उक्तौ? (c) Why does the lesson's title call the guarding of a deposit कष्टम् (hard)? (d) Apply: your classmate hands you her calculator before an exam and it is stolen from your bag. Using the dharma of न्यास from this lesson, state the two things you should do.
questions.answer: (a) A न्यासः (also called निक्षेपः) is a deposit — valuables entrusted by one person to another for safekeeping, to be returned on demand; accepting it means accepting a sacred trust (विश्वास). (b) Two duties: तं प्राणवत् रक्षेत् — guard it like one's own life; and नष्टे सति स्वधनेन मूल्यं प्रत्यर्पयेत् — if it is lost, make good its value from one's own wealth. (c) Because the keeper gains nothing yet bears all the risk: he must guard another's property like his own life, faces suspicion first if it is lost (especially if he is poor, like Charudatta), and must repay it at his own cost — responsibility without reward is the hardest burden. (d) Applying न्यासधर्म: first, tell her the truth at once, honestly and without excuses — do not hide the loss; second, make it good — replace the calculator or repay its value from my own money, as Charudatta repaid the deposit with Dhuta's ratnavali.
questions.explanation: Applies the lesson's central concept — the twofold dharma of the deposit-keeper and the meaning of the title — to a present-day situation, as NYA-03 requires.
